name: Barbell Reverse-Grip Row
summary: A bent-over compound barbell row performed with a supinated grip to place greater emphasis on the lats and biceps.

setup: Stand with feet hip-width apart and grip the barbell with an underhand (supinated) grip at shoulder width.
Hinge at the hips with a slight bend in the knees, leaning the torso forward between 45 and 70 degrees while maintaining a neutral spine.
Let the barbell hang directly below the shoulders with elbows fully extended and core braced.
steps: Initiate the pull by driving your elbows back and up toward your hips.
Pull the bar smoothly until it touches your lower abdomen or upper waistline, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause momentarily at the top of the contraction.
Lower the barbell under control back to the starting hanging position, allowing the arms to fully extend without rounding the spine.
instructions.breathing: Inhale and brace your abdominal wall before pulling, and exhale as you lower the weight or complete the rep.
cues: Drive your elbows to your back pockets.
Keep your chest proud and spine rigid.
Pull with your back, not just your arms.

common_faults.fault: Using excessive momentum or standing up during the pull.
common_faults.correction: Maintain a fixed torso angle throughout the set and reduce the load if necessary.
Keep the elbows tucked close to the sides of your torso to emphasize the lats and protect the shoulders.

common_faults.fault: Rounding the lumbar spine under load.
common_faults.correction: Brace the abdominals, set the hips back, and keep the chest lifted to preserve a neutral spine.

precautions: Avoid violently jerking the bar from the bottom position to minimize strain on the distal biceps tendon.
Halt the set if spinal alignment cannot be maintained.
